title: ITIL in Plain English: Create and Sustain Value Through Products and Services
summary: Build a current ITIL Version 5 mental model for digital product and service management, value co-creation and continual improvement.
plain_language_explanation: Current ITIL treats digital products and services as value systems that must be designed, delivered, operated and improved across their lifecycle. ITIL Version 5 keeps familiar service-management strengths while expanding product, experience, sustainability and AI-aware thinking.

title: ITIL Value System, Guiding Principles and Four Dimensions
summary: Use the ITIL Value System, guiding principles and four dimensions to reason about digital products and services holistically.
body_outline: Define value through outcomes, costs, risks, experience and sustainability.
Apply the ITIL guiding principles as decision heuristics rather than rigid steps.
Use the four dimensions: organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, and value streams and processes.
Understand governance, value-chain activity and continual improvement as connected parts of the ITIL Value System.
Identify service-consumer and provider responsibilities in value co-creation.
Tailor practices to context instead of copying process templates mechanically.

title: Incident, Problem, Change and Service-Level Management in Modern ITSM
summary: Connect operational practices without confusing restoration, root-cause reduction, risk-controlled change and service-level outcomes.
body_outline: Restore normal service quickly during incidents while preserving evidence for later analysis.
Use problem management to reduce the likelihood or impact of recurring incidents by identifying causes, workarounds and known errors.
Use change enablement to balance beneficial change with risk and operational readiness.
Set service levels around business-relevant outcomes, utility, warranty and experience rather than only technical metrics.
Connect monitoring/events, service desk, requests, releases, deployment and configuration evidence to the operating model.
Avoid process handoffs that optimize individual queues while damaging end-to-end service value.

title: Continual Improvement, Experience, Resilience and Modern ITIL Governance
summary: Use evidence, stakeholder outcomes and governance to evolve services in complex, AI-enabled environments.
architecture_notes: ITIL Version 5 evolves ITIL toward integrated digital product and service management in AI-enabled environments while retaining continual improvement and service-management discipline. Mature practice connects governance, customer/user experience, resilience, supplier dependencies, product/service lifecycle evidence and measurable outcomes rather than optimizing isolated process KPIs.

title: Read-Only ITSM Service Health Evidence Pack
summary: Build a timestamped service-management dossier without changing incidents, changes, SLAs, monitoring or production services.
steps: Identify the digital service, owner, consumers and business outcome under review.
Review open and recent incidents, recurring problems, known errors and major changes.
Review service-level targets, user-experience evidence and availability/performance trends.
Map critical suppliers, dependencies and configuration evidence relevant to the service.
Review current continual-improvement items and whether their outcomes are measured.
Document evidence gaps, risks and recommended next actions without approving or implementing change.
expected_result: A read-only service-health dossier linking value, incidents, problems, changes, service levels, experience, dependencies and improvement opportunities.
rollback: Not required; prescribed activities are read-only.

title: ITSM Decision Tree: Restore, Diagnose, Govern and Improve
summary: Separate incident restoration, problem analysis, change risk, service-level impact and continual improvement before taking action.
diagnostic_order: Confirm user/business impact and whether immediate service restoration is required.
Build an evidence timeline across incidents, events, changes and dependencies.
Separate restoration action from root-cause investigation and longer-term improvement.
Check whether an existing known error, workaround, service-level commitment or approved change path applies.
Assess whether supplier, configuration, capacity, security or architecture dependencies are contributing.
Escalate service-affecting changes through approved change and incident authority rather than bypassing governance.
escalation_boundary: Do not alter production, close records prematurely, downgrade severity, change SLAs or bypass change authority merely to make service-management metrics appear healthy.

title: ITIL / IT Service Management Foundations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering value systems, operational practices, service levels and continual improvement.

assessment_items.question: What is the first goal of incident management during a major outage?
assessment_items.answer: Restore normal service as quickly as appropriate while preserving the evidence and governance needed for follow-up analysis.

assessment_items.question: Why is problem management different from incident management?
assessment_items.answer: Problem management focuses on actual or potential causes, workarounds and known errors to reduce recurrence or impact rather than only restoring service.

assessment_items.question: Why can a technically green service still fail its service-management objective?
assessment_items.answer: Users may still experience poor outcomes, experience, risk, cost or unmet service-level commitments even when infrastructure metrics are healthy.

assessment_items.question: What makes continual improvement credible?
assessment_items.answer: A defined current state, desired outcome, measurable evidence, ownership, implemented change and verification that the change improved value or capability.

title: Senior ITIL / Service Management Interview: Value, Operations and Improvement
summary: Senior scenarios testing service restoration, problem/change governance, service levels, lifecycle thinking and measurable improvement.

questions.question: A recurring incident is repeatedly restored with the same workaround. What would you change?
answer_points: prioritize permanent remediation by impact and risk

questions.question: A service meets infrastructure availability but users report poor experience. How do you respond?
How do you challenge an emergency change during an incident?
answer_points: verify service and monitor after implementation
